description: Composite four-panel EBSD figure of a low-density 8.5Mn-6Al-XSi-0.2C (wt.%) alloy annealed 136 s, comparing 800 °C (a, c) with 1000 °C (b, d); every panel carries a "10 µm" scale bar. (a) Band-contrast (BC) map with austenite highlighted in red at 800 °C: horizontally banded, strongly elongated red austenite stringers embedded in a grey ferrite matrix, separated by thick black unindexed bands; large grey grains with faint boundaries occupy the top and bottom of the field. (b) Same BC + red-austenite colouring at 1000 °C: austenite now forms coarse, blocky, equiaxed red grains distributed through a fully recrystallised-looking grey matrix with clear continuous grain boundaries. (c) BC + inverse pole figure (IPF) map of ferrite at 800 °C: a bimodal structure of a few large, comparatively uniformly coloured interior grains and dense bands of fine, multi-coloured (randomly oriented) ferrite grains — the pancake morphology plus incomplete recrystallisation. (d) BC + IPF of ferrite at 1000 °C: uniformly equiaxed, irregularly shaped ferrite grains with strongly varied IPF colours and thick black unindexed boundaries. The panels together demonstrate that raising the annealing temperature from 800 to 1000 °C converts a banded, partially recrystallised structure into a coarser equiaxed one.

subfigures.description: EBSD band-contrast map with austenite in red, 800 °C/136 s: elongated red austenite stringers lying along horizontal bands within grey ferrite, separated by black unindexed bands; 10 µm scale bar.
EBSD band-contrast map with austenite in red, 1000 °C/136 s: coarse equiaxed/blocky red austenite grains dispersed in a grey ferrite matrix with clearly delineated grain boundaries; 10 µm scale bar.

BC + IPF map of ferrite, 800 °C/136 s: large elongated interior ferrite grains of near-uniform colour together with dense bands of fine, differently coloured grains, i.e. a pancaked and incompletely recrystallised structure; 10 µm scale bar.
BC + IPF map of ferrite, 1000 °C/136 s: equiaxed ferrite grains of mixed IPF colours with thick dark unindexed boundaries, no residual banding; 10 µm scale bar.

observations.observation: All four panels carry an identical scale bar labelled "10 µm".
In (a) the austenite (red) phase is present as highly elongated stringers aligned along horizontal bands, whereas in (b) the austenite consists of coarse blocky equiaxed grains.
Panels (a) and (b) are band-contrast maps overlaid with austenite in red, while (c) and (d) are inverse-pole-figure (IPF) colour maps of ferrite.
Panel (c) shows a bimodal ferrite structure: large near-uniformly coloured grains alternating with bands of fine, variously coloured (near-randomly oriented) grains.
Panel (d) shows equiaxed ferrite grains of uniform size range with no residual banding, in contrast to the banded pancake structure of (c).
Thick black (unindexed) bands separate the elongated regions in (a) and (c) and outline grain boundaries in (b) and (d).
The figure is the EBSD characterisation of a 8.5Mn-6Al-XSi-0.2C (wt.%) alloy annealed for 136 s at 800 °C (a, c) and 1000 °C (b, d).
The caption defines the abbreviations: BC = band contrast, IPF = inverse pole figure.
The citing text states that recrystallization of ferrite is not complete at 800 °C compared with 1000 °C, citing Fig. 11a and b.

The citing text states that pancake-shaped ferrite grains are mainly observed at the lower annealing temperature and that IPF maps show a higher degree of orientation variation at the lower temperature.
The citing text mentions local misorientations that are 'not shown here', so no misorientation/KAM panel is part of this figure.

measured_quantities: alloy composition (wt.% Mn, Al, Si, C)
unreadable_items: No IPF colour legend/triangle or orientation scale is reproduced in any panel, so absolute orientation indices cannot be assigned to the colours.
No phase fraction, grain size or misorientation values are printed on any panel.
Panel (a) and (b): exact number of grains/austenite particles cannot be counted reliably because of the unindexed black regions.
